records.text: The word of the Lord that came to Zephaniah, son of Cushi, son of Gedaliah, son of Amariah, son of Hezekiah, in the days of Josiah son of Amon, king of Judah.
All the people of the land struck down all who had conspired against King Amon. The people of the land made his son Josiah king in his place.
The rest of Amon’s deeds, what he did—behold, are these not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?
They buried him in his tomb in Oza’s garden. His son Josiah became king in his place.
Let everything utterly disappear from the face of the earth, says the Lord,
And God said, “I will blot out from the face of the earth the mankind I have made, together with the cattle, the creeping things, and the birds of heaven; for I am angered that I made them.”
let humanity and livestock disappear, let birds of the sky and fish of the sea disappear, and I will remove people from the face of the earth, says the Lord.
Therefore the land will mourn and diminish with all who inhabit it, with the field’s beasts, the earth’s creeping things and heaven’s birds; the sea’s fish will disappear,
I will stretch My hand against Judah and all Jerusalem’s inhabitants, and remove from this place the names of Baal and the names of the priests,

The king commanded Chelkias the high priest, the priests of the second rank, and the doorpost guards to bring out of the Lord’s sanctuary all the vessels made for Baal, for the grove, and for all heaven’s host. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the sademoth of Kidron and took their dust to Bethel.

He put an end to the chomarim whom Judah’s kings had appointed, who burned incense at the high places and in Judah’s cities and the places around Jerusalem, and to those burning incense to Baal, the sun, the moon, the mazouroth, and all heaven’s host.
those worshiping the army of heaven on rooftops, those swearing by the Lord and those swearing by their king,

And Jerusalem’s houses and the houses of Judah’s kings will be like the collapsing place of uncleannesses, in all the houses where they burned incense upon their roofs to all the host of the heavens and poured drink offerings to foreign gods.
those turning away from the Lord, those who did not seek the Lord and those who did not hold fast to the Lord.
Israel’s arrogance will be humbled before his face, yet they did not return to the Lord their God or seek Him in all these things.
Revere the Lord God, for the Lord’s day is near. The Lord has prepared His sacrifice and consecrated His invited guests.
The Lord’s sword was filled with blood, thickened with lambs’ fat and the fat of male goats and rams, for the Lord has a sacrifice in Bosor and a great slaughter in Idumea.
The stout ones will fall with them, and rams and bulls; the earth will become drunk with blood and be filled with their fat.
For it is the Lord’s day of judgment and a year of repayment for Zion’s judgment.
On the day of the Lord’s sacrifice I will exact judgment upon the rulers, the king’s house and all wearing foreign clothes.
Thus says the Lord: Go and descend to the house of Judah’s king and speak this word there,
and say: Hear the Lord’s word, king of Judah who sits on David’s throne—you, your household, your people, and those entering these gates.

Thus says the Lord: Do justice and righteousness; rescue the plundered from the hand of the one wronging him. Do not oppress the newcomer, orphan, or widow, and do not act impiously or shed innocent blood in this place.
Because if you truly carry out this word, kings sitting upon David’s throne and riding chariots and horses will enter this house’s gates—they, their servants, and their people.
But if you do not carry out these words, I swear by Myself, says the Lord, that this house will become a desolation.
On that day I will openly exact judgment upon everyone at the gateways, those filling the house of the Lord their God with impiety and deceit.
and murder and commit adultery and steal and swear unjustly, and you burned incense to Baal and followed foreign gods whom you do not know, to your own harm,
and you came and stood before Me in the house over which My name has been called and said, ‘We have kept away, so as not to do all these abominations,’
is My house, over which My name has been called there, a robbers’ cave before you? And behold, I have seen, says the Lord.
On that day, says the Lord, there will be a cry from the gate of those who pierce, a wail from the second quarter and a great crashing from the hills.

Therefore thus says the Lord God Almighty: “In every square there will be mourning, and in every road it will be said, ‘Alas, alas!’ A farmer will be called to mourning and lamentation and to those skilled in wailing,
and in every road there will be mourning, because I will pass through your midst,” said the Lord.
Lament, inhabitants of the battered place, for all the people of Canaan have been made alike; all exalted by silver have been destroyed.
Come now, you rich people: weep and howl over the miseries coming upon you.
Your riches have rotted, and your garments have become moth-eaten.
Your gold and silver have corroded, and their corrosion will be a testimony against you and will devour your flesh like fire. You have stored up treasure in the last days.
On that day I will search Jerusalem with a lamp and exact judgment upon men contemptuous about their safeguards, who say in their hearts, “The Lord will certainly do neither good nor harm.”
For he said in his heart, “God has forgotten; He turned His face away so as never to see.”
Arise, Lord God; let Thy hand be raised; do not forget the needy.
For what reason did the ungodly provoke God? For he said in his heart, “He will not call to account.”
Their strength will become plunder and their houses destruction. They will build houses but certainly not inhabit them, plant vineyards but certainly not drink their wine.
You shall take a wife, and another man shall have her; you shall build a house, and shall not dwell therein; you shall plant a vineyard, and shall not gather its fruit.

Therefore, because you struck the poor with fists and accepted choice gifts from them, you built houses of polished stone but certainly will not inhabit them; you planted desirable vineyards but certainly will not drink their wine.
For the Lord’s great day is near, near and very swift. The sound of the Lord’s day is bitter and harsh; it is appointed mighty.
“Alas, alas, alas for the day! For the Lord’s day is near, and it will come like suffering from suffering.”
That day is a day of wrath, a day of affliction and constraint, a day of untimely ruin and destruction, a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist,

a day of darkness and gloom, a day of cloud and mist. Like dawn a numerous and strong people will be poured over the mountains. Its like has never existed, nor will another follow it through the years, for generations upon generations.
a day of trumpet and shouting against fortified cities and high corners.
Blow a trumpet in Zion! Proclaim on My holy mountain, and let all who inhabit the land be thrown into turmoil, because the Lord’s day is present; it is near,
I will press people hard, and they will walk like the blind because they sinned against the Lord. He will pour out their blood like dust and their flesh like dung.
The Lord smite you with madness, and with blindness, and with bewilderment of mind.
And you shall grope at noonday, as the blind gropes in darkness, and He shall not prosper your ways; and you shall be wronged and plundered all your days, and there shall be none to help you.

Their silver and gold will certainly not rescue them on the day of the Lord’s wrath. In the fire of His jealousy all the earth will be consumed, for He will bring completion and haste upon all the earth’s inhabitants.

Their silver will be thrown into the broad streets, and their gold will be disregarded. Their lives certainly will not be satisfied, nor their bellies filled, because it became torment for their injustices.

Therefore wait for Me, says the Lord, for the day of My rising for testimony. My judgment is for assemblies of nations, to receive kings and pour all My furious wrath upon them; for all the earth will be consumed in My jealous fire.
Gather and bind yourselves together, O undisciplined nation,
Blow a trumpet in Zion! Consecrate a fast; proclaim a service.
Gather the people; consecrate the congregation. Choose elders; gather infants nursing at breasts. Let the bridegroom leave his bedroom and the bride her bridal chamber.

In the midst of the altar’s platform the priests who minister to the Lord will weep and say, “Spare Thy people, Lord, and do not give Thine inheritance to reproach, for nations to rule over them, so that they do not say among the nations, ‘Where is their God?’”
before you become like a passing flower, before the Lord’s wrath comes upon you, before the day of the Lord’s fury comes upon you.
A voice says, “Cry out!” And I said, “What shall I cry?” All flesh is grass, and all the glory of man is as the flower of grass.
The grass has withered, and the flower has fallen;
but the word of our God remains for ever.
Seek the Lord, all the humble of the earth; practice judgment, seek righteousness and answer these things, so that you may be sheltered on the day of the Lord’s wrath.
Seek the good and not the evil, so that you may live; then the Lord God Almighty will be with you, just as you said,
“We have hated evil things and loved good things.” Restore judgment at the gates, so that the Lord God Almighty may have mercy on Joseph’s remaining ones.
For Gaza will be plundered and Ashkelon will disappear; Ashdod will be cast out at midday and Ekron uprooted.
Thus says the Lord: “For three impieties of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn away from them, because they took Solomon’s captives into captivity, to shut them up in Idumea.
I will send fire upon Gaza’s walls, and it will devour her foundations.
I will destroy inhabitants from Azotus, and a tribe will be removed from Ascalon. I will bring My hand against Accaron, and the remaining foreigners will perish,” says the Lord.
Woe to the seacoast’s inhabitants, sojourners of Cretans! The Lord’s word is against you, Canaan, land of foreigners: I will destroy you from your dwelling.
Therefore thus says the Lord: Because the foreigners acted in vengeance and stirred up vengeance, rejoicing from their soul to wipe out for ever,
therefore thus says the Lord: Behold, I will stretch My hand against the foreigners, utterly destroy Cretans and make the remaining inhabitants of the coast perish.
I will execute great acts of vengeance upon them. They will recognize that I am the Lord when I bring My vengeance upon them.”
Crete will become pasture for flocks and an enclosure for sheep,
The utterance against Damascus. Behold, Damascus will be removed from the cities and become a ruin,
abandoned for everlasting time, a bed and resting place for flocks, with no one pursuing.

and the seacoast will belong to the remnant of Judah’s house. They will graze upon them in Ashkelon’s houses; at evening they will lodge away from the sons of Judah, for the Lord their God has visited them and turned their captivity.
I will reverse the captivity of My people Israel. They will build ruined cities and inhabit them, plant vineyards and drink their wine, plant gardens and eat their fruit.
I heard Moab’s reproaches and the Ammonites’ blows, with which they reproached My people and exalted themselves against My borders.

and say to Ammon’s sons, ‘Hear the Lord’s word! Thus says the Lord: Because you rejoiced over My holy things when they were profaned, over Israel’s land when it was devastated, and over Judah’s house when they went into captivity,

therefore behold, I am handing you to the sons of Kedem as an inheritance. They will camp with their equipment in you and set their dwellings in you. They will eat your fruits and drink your richness.
I will make Ammon’s city pastures for camels, and Ammon’s sons a pasture for sheep. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
For thus says the Lord: Because you clapped your hand and made noise with your foot, and rejoiced from your soul over Israel’s land,

therefore I will stretch My hand against you, give you to plunder among the nations, utterly destroy you from the peoples and make you perish from the countries with destruction. You will recognize that I am the Lord.’
Thus says the Lord: Because Moab said, ‘Behold, Israel’s and Judah’s house is like all the nations,’
therefore behold, I am paralyzing Moab’s shoulder from its frontier cities, the choice land, the house of Asimouth above a spring of a coastal city.
To Kedem’s sons, against Ammon’s sons, I have given them as an inheritance, so that no remembrance of Ammon’s sons may remain.
I will exact vengeance upon Moab, and they will recognize that I am the Lord.

triples.rationale: Zephaniah announces the disappearance of everything from the earth; Genesis announces the removal of humanity together with animals and birds. The shared scope is a judgment pattern, without identifying the two events.

triples.rationale: Zephaniah includes humanity, livestock, birds and fish in the announced disappearance; Hosea describes the land mourning with beasts, birds and even sea fish failing. Both extend judgment beyond human society.

triples.rationale: Zephaniah identifies those worshiping heaven's army on rooftops; Jeremiah identifies roofs where offerings were made to heaven's army. The link concerns rooftop worship, not an identification of Zephaniah's separate oath by their king.

triples.rationale: Zephaniah condemns turning away and failing to seek or hold fast to the Lord; Hosea says the people did not return to the Lord or seek Him while announcing the humbling of their arrogance.

triples.rationale: Zephaniah announces the near day and a sacrifice prepared by the Lord; Isaiah presents the Lord's sacrifice in Bosor in the setting of His judgment day. The sacrificial imagery belongs to judgment in both.

triples.rationale: Zephaniah locates cries, wailing and crashing in the city's quarters and hills; Amos announces lamentation in public ways and streets when the Lord passes through. Both make judgment audible in communal spaces.

triples.rationale: Zephaniah calls for lament because those exalted by silver are destroyed; James tells the rich to weep over coming miseries and describes gold and silver becoming testimony against them.

triples.relationship: denial of divine concern or accountability challenged
triples.rationale: Zephaniah exposes hearts saying the Lord will do neither good nor harm before announcing His searching judgment; the psalm challenges the wicked person's belief that God forgets and will not call to account and calls on God to remember the needy.

triples.relationship: covenant curse of building without inhabiting and planting without enjoyment
triples.rationale: Zephaniah says houses will be built without being inhabited and vineyards planted without their wine being drunk; Deuteronomy's curse likewise denies enjoyment of a built house and planted vineyard.
triples.source_text: Their strength will become plunder and their houses destruction. They will build houses but certainly not inhabit them, plant vineyards but certainly not drink their wine.

target_units.text: You shall take a wife, and another man shall have her; you shall build a house, and shall not dwell therein; you shall plant a vineyard, and shall not gather its fruit.

triples.relationship: prophetic repetition of uninhabited houses and undrunk vineyard wine
triples.rationale: Zephaniah's denial of dwelling in newly built houses and drinking planted vineyards' wine closely matches Amos's judgment against oppressors who built houses and planted desirable vineyards.

triples.relationship: nearness of the Lord's day
triples.rationale: Zephaniah declares the Lord's great day near and very swift; Joel laments that the Lord's day is near and comes with affliction. The correspondence concerns imminence and distress.

triples.relationship: the Lord's day described by darkness, gloom, cloud and mist
triples.rationale: Zephaniah calls the day one of darkness and gloom, cloud and mist; Joel uses the same cluster of dark-weather descriptions for the approaching day.

triples.rationale: Zephaniah describes a day of trumpet and shouting against fortifications; Joel orders a trumpet in Zion and a proclamation on the holy mountain because the Lord's day approaches. Both connect alarm with the day, without equating their city details.

triples.rationale: Zephaniah says silver and gold cannot rescue on the wrath day; Ezekiel describes silver thrown into streets and gold disregarded, unable to satisfy life or fill bellies. Both expose precious metals' failure under judgment, though Ezekiel's stated failure concerns sustenance.

triples.rationale: The opening oracle says the earth will be consumed in the fire of God's jealousy; the later oracle repeats that all the earth will be consumed by His jealous fire when nations are assembled for wrath.

triples.relationship: the passing flower as an image of transience
triples.rationale: Zephaniah urges action before becoming like a passing flower and before wrath; Isaiah likens human glory to grass's flower that falls while God's word remains. The shared flower image emphasizes the fragility underlying Zephaniah's urgency.

triples.relationship: seeking good and practicing judgment in hope of mercy
triples.rationale: Zephaniah calls the humble to seek the Lord and righteousness and practice judgment in hope of shelter; Amos urges seeking good and restoring judgment in hope of the Lord's mercy upon the remnant.
triples.source_text: Seek the Lord, all the humble of the earth; practice judgment, seek righteousness and answer these things, so that you may be sheltered on the day of the Lord’s wrath.

triples.relationship: parallel judgment against the named coastal cities
triples.rationale: Zephaniah names Gaza, Ashkelon, Ashdod and Ekron in judgment; Amos's oracle names Gaza, Ascalon, Azotus and Accaron. The overlapping set of coastal cities is preserved with each passage's different native spellings and punishments.

triples.relationship: judgment against Cretans and coastal inhabitants
triples.rationale: Zephaniah addresses the coastal Cretans and announces destruction of their dwelling; Ezekiel announces the destruction of Cretans and the coast's remaining inhabitants. Both locate the threatened population by the coast.
triples.source_text: Woe to the seacoast’s inhabitants, sojourners of Cretans! The Lord’s word is against you, Canaan, land of foreigners: I will destroy you from your dwelling.

triples.relationship: ruined territory becoming pasture for flocks
triples.rationale: Zephaniah says Crete will become pasture and a sheep enclosure; Isaiah describes ruined Damascus as an abandoned resting place for flocks. The connection is the reversal from inhabited strength to grazing land, not identity of the places.

triples.relationship: reversal of captivity associated with restored habitation
triples.rationale: Zephaniah assigns the coast and houses of Ashkelon to the remnant and says the Lord visits and turns captivity; Amos promises to reverse Israel's captivity so they inhabit rebuilt cities. The shared restoration does not erase Zephaniah's unusual lodging clause.
triples.source_text: and the seacoast will belong to the remnant of Judah’s house. They will graze upon them in Ashkelon’s houses; at evening they will lodge away from the sons of Judah, for the Lord their God has visited them and turned their captivity.

target_units.text: I will reverse the captivity of My people Israel. They will build ruined cities and inhabit them, plant vineyards and drink their wine, plant gardens and eat their fruit.

triples.relationship: Moab and Ammon condemned for hostility toward God's people
triples.rationale: Zephaniah cites Moab's reproaches and Ammon's blows and boasts against the people's borders; Ezekiel condemns Ammon's rejoicing over Israel's devastation and Moab's disparaging comparison of Israel and Judah with other nations.
triples.source_text: I heard Moab’s reproaches and the Ammonites’ blows, with which they reproached My people and exalted themselves against My borders.

target_units.text: and say to Ammon’s sons, ‘Hear the Lord’s word! Thus says the Lord: Because you rejoiced over My holy things when they were profaned, over Israel’s land when it was devastated, and over Judah’s house when they went into captivity,

therefore behold, I am handing you to the sons of Kedem as an inheritance. They will camp with their equipment in you and set their dwellings in you. They will eat your fruits and drink your richness.
I will make Ammon’s city pastures for camels, and Ammon’s sons a pasture for sheep. You will recognize that I am the Lord.
For thus says the Lord: Because you clapped your hand and made noise with your foot, and rejoiced from your soul over Israel’s land,

therefore I will stretch My hand against you, give you to plunder among the nations, utterly destroy you from the peoples and make you perish from the countries with destruction. You will recognize that I am the Lord.’
Thus says the Lord: Because Moab said, ‘Behold, Israel’s and Judah’s house is like all the nations,’
therefore behold, I am paralyzing Moab’s shoulder from its frontier cities, the choice land, the house of Asimouth above a spring of a coastal city.
To Kedem’s sons, against Ammon’s sons, I have given them as an inheritance, so that no remembrance of Ammon’s sons may remain.
I will exact vengeance upon Moab, and they will recognize that I am the Lord.
